_comment: Houdini RFSoC single-UE client, slot-granular native-TDD demo. BS arms a 30-symbol TDD ring built from frame_schedule (one 4096-tick symbol per slot, '6' beacon strobe on the B slot, rx on every other slot -- a gate close would abandon the continuous capture, see DEMO_VERIFICATION.md). The beacon is a SINGLE 496-sample core per frame at slot_start+384 (strobe offs), played from the TX replay RAM with explicit zeros to the window close. UE: stamp-based hunt -> confirm(x2) -> anchor acquisition with a 20 dB sync-SNR floor (HOUDINI_SYNC_SNR_DB), resync = gated drift tracking. Run procedure: CSI_DEMO_WALKTHROUGH.md; evidence ledger: DEMO_VERIFICATION.md. Matched-NCO Zone-1: TX ch1 -> RX ch1, NCO 500 MHz. 30 slots x 4096 = 122880 samps = EXACTLY 1 ms per frame = 320 steps of the 384-tick TX grid, so per-frame snap residuals are constant within a run.
_ue_tdd_pilot_note: UE streams its pilot with the tdd=1 TX stream arg -> the driver TxTickAnchor accepts beacon-referenced starts on the 3.125us/384-tick TDD grid (SH-248/SH-301). ue_tx_advance_ticks is the fine calibration seating the pilot in the BS rx window; tx_advance needs re-derivation after the grid-model fix (DEMO_VERIFICATION.md 4.29/4.31: measure pilot_grid_off, set tx_advance to land it).
_bs_hw_framer_note: true selects the BS native-Houdini-TDD framer path. The TDD symbol now EQUALS the sounder slot (4096 ticks; the old 0.5 ms symbol and its multi-copy beacon fill are retired, DEMO_VERIFICATION.md 4.12/4.16). samps_per_slot must stay <= 4096 (FPGA TX_RAM depth).
_corr_scale_init_note: Acquisition-only detection threshold; SMALLER is STRICTER (test: corr_scale * peak > trailing local energy). The 2026-08 measured populations (no-beacon 3.4e-07, beacon 0.31..4.2) were taken in the multi-copy-beacon era; acquisition now ALSO requires the 20 dB in-window SNR floor and two grid-consistent confirms, which is what actually rejects the noise-artifact class (DEMO_VERIFICATION.md 4.25/4.32). Re-sync uses corr_scale and relaxes per retry, gated by the same floor.
